info.bio: Los ingleses X-Ray Spex fueron una banda de punk rock formados en 1976. Con la extraordinaria cantante Poly Styrene (a.k.a. Marion Elliot) vocalizando, Jak Airport (Jack Stafford) en guitarras, Paul Dean en bajo, Paul ‘B. P.’ Hurding en batería, y Lora Logic (a.k.a. Susan Whitby, quien después lideró Essential Logic) en saxofón. Este último instrumento nombrado fue una adición totalmente atípica a la instrumentación del punk rock tradicional del momento

scenes.name: Punk rock (1976-77)
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: El «Año Cero»: hacia el verano de 1977 el punk ya era una parodia de sí mismo y su frágil alianza entre chicos obreros y bohemios de escuela de arte se rompe. De un lado quedan los «punks verdaderos», populistas, que desembocarán en el Oi! y el hardcore; del otro, la vanguardia que se llamará postpunk, que vio en 1977 no un retorno al rock crudo sino la ocasión de romper con la tradición. Su legado común: la fe en el poder de la música y el «hazlo tú mismo».
scenes.family: Antecedentes: punk, art rock, kraut y glam

scenes.name: Dark punk y rock gótico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk británico estuvo flanqueado desde el principio por un movimiento «gótico» que canalizaba su violencia hacia atmósferas de terror y rituales esotéricos: Stranglers, Siouxsie, X-Ray Spex. Lo más interesante evita el tono de película de terror: The Cure introducen la angustia existencial de Camus y Sartre (Pornography, Disintegration); Joy Division mezclan Doors, Kraftwerk y Black Sabbath y su final anuncia el synth-pop; Bauhaus, Killing Joke, Psychedelic Furs, los irlandeses Virgin Prunes y la cima del género, Public Image Ltd de Johnny Lydon, que convierte el punk en música de cámara con dub y ecos étnicos (Second Edition, Flowers Of Romance). Después, el gótico bailable de Sisters Of Mercy, Alien Sex Fiend, Cult, Mission e In The Nursery.

xref.title: Entry into 1970s Punk Scene (1976)
xref.body: Born Marion Joan Elliott Saeed in South London, Poly Styrene was drawn into the 1970s punk scene after witnessing a Sex Pistols performance in the summer of 1976. Following an attempt at a solo career, she formed the band X-Ray Spex and adopted her distinctive stage name, which she described as a "fake plastic name." "She was from South London and also got sucked into the 1970s punk scene after seeing the sex pistols in the summer of 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Career Impact and Fans
xref.body: While neither X-Ray Spex nor her solo career produced numerous hits, Paulie Styrin earned considerable respect from influential figures in music, including U2, who were major fans of her work. "And while neither X-Ray Specks or her solo career produced a lot of hits, Paulie earned a lot of respect from some big names. You too was on record as being a major fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Black Female Punk Band Frontperson (Probable)
xref.body: Polly Styrene, the singer for Britain's X-Ray Spex, is identified as one of the original punks and was probably the first Black female front person for a punk band. "She was probably the first Black female front person for a punk band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Identity and Punk Entry
xref.body: Born Marion Joan Elliott Saeed in South London, she adopted the stage name Paulie Styrin, which she described as a "fake plastic name." Her entry into the 1970s punk scene was prompted by seeing the Sex Pistols perform in the summer of 1976, after which she formed X-Ray Spex following an attempt at a solo career. "Her real name was Marion Joan Elliott Saeed. She was from South London and also got second to the 1970s punk scene after seeing the Sex Pistols in the summer of 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inspirational Figure and Peer Respect
xref.body: Despite X-Ray Spex and her solo career not producing many hits, Poly Styrene became a significant inspiration to many who attended her shows. She earned considerable respect from influential figures, including Bono of U2, who publicly acknowledged himself as a major fan. "And that's why she was such an inspiration to so many who came out to see her play back in the day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Punk Pioneer
xref.body: Poly Styrene of X-Ray Spex was a pioneer who embodied punk rock values, inspiring many to express themselves regardless of background or gender. "Suzy Su, of Suzy in the Banshee's, members of the Slitz, Pauli Styrene of X-Ray Specks, Chrissy Hinder, the Pretenders, Patty Smith, and so many more. They were all pioneers and they all inspired many people, women, but also men, to do what they did."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
